question: Should QQBot permanently reject inbound gateway messages above 1 MiB, or use a larger channel-specific cap such as 16 MiB?
rationale: The patch correctly strengthens the resource boundary, but upstream QQ documentation does not specify a maximum event size; choosing the value trades memory exposure against the possibility of dropping legitimate future gateway events.

options.title: Approve the 1 MiB cap
options.body: Accept the contributor's proven 1 MiB boundary as appropriate for QQ's JSON and URL-metadata event model, while explicitly owning the compatibility risk.

options.title: Raise the cap
options.body: Use a larger fixed bound such as 16 MiB to retain substantial protection over the 100 MiB dependency default while reducing legitimate-event rejection risk.

options.title: Pause for protocol evidence
options.body: Hold the PR until QQBot owners can provide an authoritative event-size limit or representative production-size evidence.

recommendation.title: Approve the 1 MiB cap
recommendation.body: Accept the contributor's proven 1 MiB boundary as appropriate for QQ's JSON and URL-metadata event model, while explicitly owning the compatibility risk.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available feature-history owner for the QQBot gateway implementation and its event-shape assumptions.
